defects.what: tests/unit/council.test.ts will fail against the rebuild for two independent reasons, and the second one is caused by the convention this foundation file establishes. (Types-match cross-check itself: 0 mismatches — see notes above.)
defects.evidence: tests/unit/council.test.ts:231-233 does readFileSync(join(__dirname, '../../supabase/migrations/20260704080000_create_council_sessions.sql')). That path no longer exists — supabase/migrations/ now contains only _archive/, per supabase/migrations/_archive/README.md ('the rebuild ships a single clean baseline instead'). Verified: `npx vitest run tests/unit/council.test.ts` -> 'Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open /home/user/dikagustiana.com/supabase/migrations/20260704080000_create_council_sessions.sql', 1 failed suite, 0 tests collected, so `npm run test:unit` is red. Second, even after repointing the path, the assertion at tests/unit/council.test.ts:244 is expect(policy).toMatch(/has_role\(auth\.uid\(\), 'admin'\)/) — the baseline's stated house style, applied throughout this file (e.g. WITH CHECK (public.has_role((SELECT auth.uid()), 'admin')) on user_roles_insert_admin), writes has_role((SELECT auth.uid()), 'admin'), which that regex does not match. The same test's `expect(sql).not.toMatch(/USING\s*\(\s*true\s*\)/i)` is also a text assertion over a file that no longer exists in that form. This is outside the foundation file's own scope (council_sessions is a later part) but it is absent from the author's open-risk list, which only mentions council_sessions as 'still needs to be honoured by the other baseline parts'.
defects.fix: Repoint the guardrail test at the baseline file(s) that actually own council_sessions and relax the regex to accept the initplan form, e.g. /has_role\(\s*\(?\s*(SELECT\s+)?auth\.uid\(\)\s*\)?\s*,\s*'admin'\s*\)/ plus the inlined EXISTS-on-user_roles form; better still, replace the text-matching test with a live RLS probe in tests/live/ so it cannot rot against SQL formatting. Whoever authors the council_sessions part should own this, but it should be recorded as a rebuild task now.

defects.what: The file's 'KNOWN AND ACCEPTED LIMIT' block and the matching author decision overstate what admin role-granting can do over PostgREST: 'admin INSERT works over PostgREST' holds only for a bare insert (Prefer: return=minimal). The idiomatic supabase-js shape .insert(...).select() fails outright, not silently.
defects.evidence: Reproduced on a Supabase-shaped PG16 harness with this exact file applied. As role authenticated with request.jwt.claim.sub set to the admin uuid: `INSERT INTO public.user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES ('...c3','admin');` -> INSERT 0 1 (works, as documented). But `INSERT INTO public.user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES ('...c3','user') RETURNING id;` -> ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table "user_roles". Cause: RETURNING makes Postgres apply SELECT policies to the new row, and the only SELECT policy on the table is user_roles_select_own (USING (user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()))), while user_roles_no_self_grant_insert forces user_id <> auth.uid() — so any row an admin is allowed to insert is by construction a row the admin cannot read back. The same probe confirmed the rest of the block is accurate: targeted UPDATE -> UPDATE 0, targeted DELETE -> DELETE 0, unqualified DELETE -> DELETE 2 (removes the admin's own row). Nothing in src/ inserts into user_roles today (grep from('user_roles') hits only src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:26 plus tests/live/adminGating.spec.ts:16,28, all reads), so this is not a live break — but .insert().select() is the shape used elsewhere in the repo (tests/live/adminGating.spec.ts:47-54 for essays), so the note as written will mislead whoever builds role administration.
defects.fix: Correct the comment to say 'a bare admin INSERT (Prefer: return=minimal) works; .insert().select() fails with an RLS violation because RETURNING applies the own-row SELECT policy to a row the self-grant guard guarantees the admin cannot see', and keep the existing recommendation to expose role administration through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC rather than adding a has_role-based SELECT policy. No SQL change needed.

defects.what: The header's enumeration of what remains to be authored omits two live, src-queried tables: public.sections and public.categories. Neither is created here and neither appears in the deferred list, so on a fresh rebuild that follows this file's plan, 7 src call sites break with 42P01 (relation does not exist).
defects.evidence: Candidate SQL header: "Content tables (essays, fsli_*, books_uploads, finance_*, council_sessions, admin_audit_log) are authored in later parts." — 'sections' and 'categories' appear nowhere in that list nor anywhere in the file. Both are real live tables: /home/user/dikagustiana.com/docs/db/import.sql:1089 `CREATE TABLE public.sections (...)` and :1102 `CREATE TABLE public.categories (...)`, and both are in the generated types (/home/user/dikagustiana.com/src/integrations/supabase/types.ts:1759 `sections:` and :110 `categories:`), so precedence rule 1 keeps them. Breaking call sites: /home/user/dikagustiana.com/src/hooks/queries/useSections.ts:21 `.from('sections').select('*').eq('is_active', true).order('sort_order')` (queryFn does `if (error) throw error`), useSections.ts:37 `.from('sections').select('*').eq('slug', slug).single()`, /home/user/dikagustiana.com/src/hooks/queries/useCategories.ts:24 `supabase.from('categories').select('*')`, useCategories.ts:43 `.from('categories').select('*').eq('slug', slug)`, /home/user/dikagustiana.com/src/domains/writing/hooks/useWriterSections.ts:10, /home/user/dikagustiana.com/src/domains/writing/hooks/useWriterCategories.ts:10, and /home/user/dikagustiana.com/src/pages/GreenTransitionPhase.tsx:141-143. The sharpest case is GreenTransitionPhase.tsx:142 `.select('id, sections!categories_section_id_fkey(slug)')` — an embedded PostgREST select that names the FK constraint literally, so it needs public.categories, public.sections AND a constraint named exactly `categories_section_id_fkey`; that name is asserted in types.ts:141 (`foreignKeyName: "categories_section_id_fkey"`) and is created in the final lines of /home/user/dikagustiana.com/supabase/migrations/_archive/20260215_001_enforce_category_hierarchy.sql (`ALTER TABLE categories ADD CONSTRAINT categories_section_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (section_id) REFERENCES sections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`). They are also structurally load-bearing for the deferred essays part: that same migration does `ALTER TABLE categories ALTER COLUMN section_id SET NOT NULL` (step 7), `ALTER TABLE essays ALTER COLUMN category_id SET NOT NULL` (step 4) and `essays_category_id_fkey ... REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (step 8), so essays cannot be authored correctly while sections/categories are unowned. Note this is a defect in this file's claim, not in the SQL it executes — I applied the DDL to a PG16 Supabase-shaped harness and every query against the tables it does own (user_roles, profiles, the three buckets) passed.
defects.fix: Correct the header enumeration to read "... essays, sections, categories, fsli_*, books_uploads, finance_*, council_sessions, admin_audit_log ..." and explicitly assign public.sections and public.categories to a later part, before essays (essays.category_id is a NOT NULL FK to categories, and categories.section_id is a NOT NULL FK to sections, so the create order must be sections -> categories -> essays). Whoever authors them must reproduce the constraint NAMES verbatim, not just the shape: `categories_section_id_fkey` and `essays_category_id_fkey`, because GreenTransitionPhase.tsx:142 addresses the relationship by constraint name and a differently-named FK yields a PostgREST PGRST200 'could not find a relationship' error rather than a silent fallback. Also carry over `sections.voice_role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (voice_role IN ('manager','economist','educator','coach','hybrid'))` (import.sql:1093) and `UNIQUE(section_id, slug)` on categories (import.sql:1111).

defects.what: public.voice_role_enum is created but has zero consumers anywhere in the target schema — it is a dead type. Non-breaking, but it shows the 'kept enums' set was derived from the types.ts Enums block (which lists every type that exists in the DB) rather than from actual column usage, which is the same derivation error that let sections/categories fall out of the table enumeration.
defects.evidence: Candidate SQL section 1 creates `public.voice_role_enum AS ENUM ('manager','economist','educator','coach','hybrid')`, sourced from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts Enums. But no column uses it. The two voice_role columns in the kept schema are both plain text: /home/user/dikagustiana.com/docs/db/import.sql:1093 `voice_role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (voice_role IN ('manager','economist','educator','coach','hybrid'))` on sections, and import.sql:1116 `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS voice_role TEXT` on essays. types.ts agrees both are plain strings: types.ts:1768 `voice_role: string` (sections) and types.ts:1791 `voice_role?: string` (essays). A grep of docs/db/import.sql for `voice_role_enum` returns exactly one hit, its own `CREATE TYPE` at import.sql:1189, with no column reference. Contrast the other three kept enums, which all have real consumers and must stay: content_status_enum (import.sql:1194 `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS status content_status_enum DEFAULT 'draft'`, matching types.ts essays `status: Database["public"]["Enums"]["content_status_enum"] | null`), lesson_type_enum (import.sql:2261 `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS lesson_type public.lesson_type_enum DEFAULT 'concept'`), and model_depth (import.sql:3457 `depth model_depth NOT NULL DEFAULT 'foundation'`).
defects.fix: Keep the CREATE TYPE (dropping it would make the regenerated types.ts diverge from the committed one, and it costs nothing), but change its comment from an implied-in-use 'kept' to an explicit note: no column references voice_role_enum; sections.voice_role and essays.voice_role are TEXT, and sections.voice_role carries a CHECK constraint with the same five values. Otherwise whoever authors the sections and essays tables will reasonably type those columns as the enum and silently break the `voice_role: string` contract in types.ts:1768/1791 and the local TS union at src/hooks/queries/useSections.ts:8.

defects.what: GRANT EXECUTE ON has_role() TO anon turns the deliberately-hidden user_roles table into a public read oracle over PostgREST, defeating the only SELECT policy on it.
defects.evidence: Candidate section 3: `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.has_role(uuid, public.app_role) TO authenticated, anon, service_role;`. has_role is SECURITY DEFINER, so its body bypasses RLS on user_roles, and src/integrations/supabase/types.ts:1820-1828 declares it under `Functions`, i.e. PostgREST exposes `POST /rest/v1/rpc/has_role`. Reproduced on PG16 with the harness: `SET ROLE anon; SELECT count(*) FROM public.user_roles;` -> 0 rows (policy working), but `SET ROLE anon; SELECT public.has_role('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1','admin');` -> `t`. An anon publishable-key holder can therefore test any UUID for admin. This directly falsifies the file's own comment on the NOTE block ("Consequence: enumerating other users' roles is a service_role / SQL-editor operation, not a PostgREST one") and it ignores the repo's own remediation plan, docs/CODE-REVIEW-2026-07-04.md:121: "has_role() executable oleh anon ... solusi jangka panjang: inline EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_roles ...) ke policy lalu re-revoke". The candidate did the inlining but skipped the re-revoke. Candidate UUIDs are not hard to come by: defect #2 below hands anon `storage.objects.owner`, which Supabase populates with the uploader's uid (i.e. the admin's).
defects.fix: Add `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.has_role(uuid, public.app_role) FROM anon;` (keep the authenticated + service_role grants, which the user_roles write policies need). I verified the anon-only revoke breaks nothing: anon storage read still returns rows, anon `SELECT count(*) FROM user_roles` still returns 0 rows rather than erroring, an anon-facing inlined-EXISTS policy on a simulated essays table still returns published rows only, and the admin user_roles INSERT still succeeds. Nothing calls it as anon either -- `grep -rn "rpc(" src/ tests/ supabase/functions/` returns zero actual call sites (the only hit is a comment at supabase/functions/council-review/index.ts:98 explaining why it is NOT used). Update the COMMENT ON FUNCTION, which currently reads as a blanket "DO NOT REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon/authenticated" and will stop a future reviewer from making this fix.

defects.what: The public_buckets_read policy grants anon SELECT on storage.objects for all three buckets. It is required by zero code paths, and it converts the unguessable random object names used for draft-essay images into an enumerable listing -- plus it discloses the admin's auth UUID.
defects.evidence: Candidate section 5: `CREATE POLICY "public_buckets_read" ON storage.objects FOR SELECT TO anon, authenticated USING (bucket_id IN ('essay-images','books','finance-models'));`. Its stated justification -- "keeping SELECT open is what makes getPublicUrl()-served assets work for anonymous visitors ... regardless of storage-api routing details" -- is false, and the repo says so itself: supabase/migrations/_archive/20260622135932_93e6af0b-465c-4404-9a24-fcf520b7c25f.sql:59 reads `-- 7. Restrict storage listing on public buckets to admins; public URLs still work`. All three buckets are inserted with `public = true`, and getPublicUrl() is a pure client-side string builder that makes no request; the served route `/storage/v1/object/public/{bucket}/{path}` does not evaluate storage.objects RLS. Every storage read in the app is getPublicUrl: src/pages/BookReader.tsx:19, src/components/editorial/ImageUploader.tsx:132-134, src/components/editorial/FigureUploader.tsx:163-165, src/components/finance-in-action/ModelAdminPanel.tsx:54, src/domains/writing/WriterStudio.tsx:224. There is no `.list()`, `.download()` or `.createSignedUrl()` anywhere in src/ or tests/. What the policy does buy an attacker: essay-image names are deliberately unguessable random tokens -- `drafts/${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}.${ext}` at src/domains/writing/WriterStudio.tsx:213, and `${folder}/...` with `const folder = section || 'drafts'` at src/components/editorial/FigureUploader.tsx:149-150 and ImageUploader.tsx:119. An open SELECT policy lets an anon key call `POST /storage/v1/object/list/essay-images` with `{"prefix":"drafts/"}` and recover every image embedded in an unpublished draft essay. The same mechanism defeats the books_uploads soft delete (its read policy is `deleted_at IS NULL`, per 20251223120457...sql, so the row is hidden but the object path is now listable and the bucket is public), and exposes finance-models paths, which are `${model.slug}/${file.name}` (ModelAdminPanel.tsx:45). It also exposes storage.objects.owner / owner_id, which storage-api populates with the uploader's uid -- feeding defect #1's oracle. Reproduced: `SET ROLE anon; SELECT count(*) FROM storage.objects;` -> 3 (every object across the three buckets).
defects.fix: Drop public_buckets_read, or narrow it to `TO authenticated` plus the same inlined `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()) AND ur.role = 'admin')` used by the write policies -- i.e. keep the 20260622135932 shape. Verified that removing anon SELECT on storage.objects regresses nothing in src/, because no read path touches the authenticated object API. If an admin file browser is built later, that admin-gated SELECT policy is the place for it.

defects.what: The three user_roles write policies ship non-functional: a targeted admin UPDATE or DELETE affects 0 rows and reports success, while the only DELETE that does work is the unqualified one that wipes the caller's own admin grant with no client-side path to recover it.
defects.evidence: Reproduced on PG16 as the seeded admin (a1): `UPDATE public.user_roles SET role='user' WHERE user_id='...c3';` -> `UPDATE 0`; `DELETE FROM public.user_roles WHERE user_id='...c3';` -> `DELETE 0`; `DELETE FROM public.user_roles;` -> `DELETE 2`, leaving the table empty including a1's own admin row. Root cause confirmed: it is the absent admin SELECT policy -- after adding `CREATE POLICY ... FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.has_role((SELECT auth.uid()),'admin'))`, the same targeted statements became `UPDATE 1` / `DELETE 1`. PostgREST always emits a WHERE from the query params (and RETURNING under `Prefer: return=representation`), so every REST-shaped role revoke hits the 0-row path and returns 204/`[]` -- a silent success. Two things the author's disclosure understates: (i) it is silent, so any future role-admin UI or manual REST revoke will report that admin was removed while nothing changed; (ii) after the unqualified DELETE, `user_roles_no_self_grant_insert` makes recovery structurally impossible from any client session -- I confirmed the now-role-less a1 session could not re-insert anything (`new row violates row-level security policy for table "user_roles"`), so the project is locked out of admin until someone reaches for service_role or the SQL editor. Note the author's stated reason for refusing the has_role SELECT policy is correct and I reproduced it: with that policy present and EXECUTE revoked, the AuthContext own-row read at src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:24-30 fails with `permission denied for function has_role`. So the answer is not to add that policy.
defects.fix: Do not ship dead policies. Either (a) ship the SECURITY DEFINER role-admin RPC the comment only promises -- one function that does its own has_role('admin') check and performs the grant/revoke with RLS bypassed, exposed to authenticated -- and drop user_roles_update_admin / user_roles_delete_admin; or (b) at minimum make the failure honest with `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON public.user_roles FROM authenticated;` alongside dropping those two policies, so the API returns `permission denied for table user_roles` instead of a 204 that changed nothing. Either way, keep user_roles_insert_admin (verified working: admin INSERT for another user succeeds) and keep the RESTRICTIVE self-grant guards.

defects.what: The GRANT block does not produce the privilege posture the file documents. Supabase's default privileges already give anon and authenticated ALL on every new public table, and GRANT only adds -- so anon ends up holding INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on user_roles and profiles, and TRUNCATE is never checked by RLS.
defects.evidence: Candidate section 3 ships `GRANT SELECT ON public.user_roles TO anon;` with the comment "anon keeps SELECT on purpose" and "RLS is the trust boundary here, not GRANTs". With Supabase's real bootstrap (`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO postgres, anon, authenticated, service_role`) reproduced in the harness, `information_schema.role_table_grants` after applying the candidate shows anon holding `DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE` on both public.user_roles and public.profiles -- identical to authenticated. The four DML verbs are indeed contained by RLS (verified: anon INSERT into user_roles -> `new row violates row-level security policy`), so this does not leak through the anon key today; PostgREST never issues TRUNCATE. But TRUNCATE bypasses RLS entirely, so the comment's blanket claim is wrong for the one verb where the GRANT layer is the only boundary, and the surrounding comment explicitly forbids the fix ("A privilege-layer revoke here would recreate failure (a) one layer down -- do not add one"), which is only true of SELECT.
defects.fix: Make the privilege layer match the documentation: `REVOKE ALL ON public.user_roles FROM anon, authenticated; GRANT SELECT ON public.user_roles TO anon; GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON public.user_roles TO authenticated;` and the same REVOKE-then-GRANT shape for public.profiles. I verified the SELECT grant to anon is genuinely load-bearing and must be kept -- with it revoked, an anon-facing policy that inlines the user_roles EXISTS check fails with `permission denied for table user_roles` instead of returning 0 rows -- so narrow the comment to SELECT rather than dropping it.

defects.what: essays.category_id is declared NOT NULL with no DEFAULT, dropping the column default that exists in the live schema. This flips the regenerated `essays.Insert.category_id` from optional to required, which breaks `tsc` in two files and breaks three content-seed migrations plus one live app write path at runtime. It is NOT covered by the sanctioned "category_id is now NOT NULL" staleness exemption — types.ts's `category_id?:` optionality is correct against live precisely because of the default.
defects.evidence: supabase/migrations/_archive/20260219_004_seed_fundamentals_lessons.sql:20-21 runs `ALTER TABLE public.essays ALTER COLUMN category_id SET DEFAULT '0f111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'::uuid;`, and no migration ever drops it (`grep -ri "drop default" supabase/ docs/db/` returns 0 hits; the archive's only three ALTER COLUMN statements are that one plus the two SET NOT NULLs). types.ts:357 declares `category_id?: string | null` in essays.Insert. VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: patching types.ts essays.Insert to `category_id: string` (what the candidate DDL regenerates) and running `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` produces TS2769 at src/components/next-big-thing/EssayDialog.tsx(138,12) "Property 'category_id' is missing ... but required" and src/hooks/queries/useAdminEssays.ts(192,17) "Property 'category_id' is missing in type 'CreateEssayData' but required"; re-patching to `category_id?: string` (NOT NULL *with* default, the live shape) exits 0 clean. types.ts was restored afterwards (git diff --stat shows only the pre-existing docs/SESSION_LOG.md change). Runtime fallout: src/components/next-big-thing/EssayDialog.tsx:138-149 is live code (routed from src/pages/TheNextBigThing.tsx:108 and src/components/next-big-thing/EssayModule.tsx:311), has no category UI, and never sends category_id -> 23502 on every new next-big-thing essay; three seed migrations insert essays with no category_id and only apply because of the default (20260301073238_cd28465a-44e8-47d1-9f8f-a83e9ad96295.sql:3, 20260301073420_35bdab28-525d-460c-bdf2-da10cbf7562d.sql:2, 20260301073540_8d5c4502-0beb-4ac3-b320-b24e9757a6f0.sql:2). The author's decision note "the live write paths ... both send it" is also wrong for src/components/writer/WriterEditor.tsx:347 (`if (categoryId) essayData.category_id = categoryId;`) because handleSave at WriterEditor.tsx:287-305 gates only *publish* on validation, so a draft save with no category selected reaches .insert() at :365 without the column; only WriterStudio.tsx:265-273 hard-blocks it.
defects.fix: Carry the live default forward, e.g. add after the essays CREATE TABLE: `ALTER TABLE public.essays ALTER COLUMN category_id SET DEFAULT '0f111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'::uuid;` (or declare it inline on the column). Also ensure the row that default points at is seeded before anything relies on it — 20260219_004_seed_fundamentals_lessons.sql:11-18 inserts the fixed-UUID 'finance-general' category into public.categories — otherwise the default merely trades the NOT NULL violation for an FK violation on essays_category_id_fkey. Separately, if the project instead wants category_id genuinely required with no default, EssayDialog.tsx:138 and WriterEditor.tsx:347 both need a category before insert and useAdminEssays.ts:178-192 (CreateEssayData/useCreateEssay) needs deleting or fixing — but that is an app change, not a baseline-parity change.

defects.what: categories.section_id is declared NOT NULL, which is a THIRD divergence from types.ts beyond the two sanctioned ones (dropped finance_fundamentals/essays.fundamental_id and essays.category_id NOT NULL). It is faithful to the live schema and non-breaking, but it is undocumented, so it will read as an unexplained diff when types are regenerated.
defects.evidence: types.ts:116 declares `section_id: string | null` in the categories Row and types.ts:126 `section_id?: string | null` in Insert; the candidate DDL declares `section_id uuid NOT NULL`. Live really is NOT NULL — supabase/migrations/_archive/20260215_001_enforce_category_hierarchy.sql:117 `ALTER TABLE categories ALTER COLUMN section_id SET NOT NULL;`. Confirmed non-breaking: patching types.ts categories.Insert to a required `section_id: string` contributed zero errors to `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` (nothing in src/ inserts or updates categories, and src/hooks/queries/useCategories.ts:6 declares its own local `section_id: string | null` interface which accepts a narrowed `string`). But docs/DB_READINESS.md:83-84 enumerates only two stale spots: "types.ts is stale: it still shows essays.fundamental_id/finance_fundamentals (dropped) and a nullable category_id (now NOT NULL)."
defects.fix: Keep the NOT NULL (it matches live) and add categories.section_id to the known-staleness note in docs/DB_READINESS.md:83-84 so the third generated-type diff is expected rather than surprising at `supabase gen types` time.

defects.what: essays.category_id uuid NOT NULL breaks the Next Big Thing admin "Add Essay" insert, which structurally cannot supply a category_id. The author's decision record asserts the only insert path missing category_id is the dead useCreateEssay and that "the live write paths ... both send it" — that audit missed this call site entirely.
defects.evidence: src/components/next-big-thing/EssayDialog.tsx:136-150 inserts into essays with exactly these keys: section, title, slug, snippet, author, date, read_time, thumbnail_url, phase, published, content. There is no category_id key and no category input in the dialog at all — the field labelled "Category" at src/components/next-big-thing/EssayDialog.tsx:208-217 is bound to formData.phase (:210-211), not to a category id. The path is live and admin-reachable: src/pages/TheNextBigThing.tsx:92-95 renders the `{isAdmin && <Button onClick={() => setDialogOpen(true)}>Add Essay</Button>}`, and :108-115 renders `<EssayDialog ... essay={null}>`, which forces isEditing=false (EssayDialog.tsx:58) and therefore the insert branch. Verified against the applied DDL on PostgreSQL 16 as the admin role: `ERROR: null value in column "category_id" of relation "essays" violates not-null constraint`. Note on parity: docs/DECISIONS.md:77-81 and supabase/migrations/_archive/20260215_001_enforce_category_hierarchy.sql:103 indicate live is also NOT NULL, so this is a pre-existing app break rather than a regression the DDL introduces — but the constraint is being accepted on the strength of a verification claim that is factually wrong.
defects.fix: Either (a) keep NOT NULL and fix the call site — add a category selector to EssayDialog and send category_id (the section is hardcoded to 'next-big-thing' at :139, so the section's default category can be resolved), or (b) if the rebuild is meant to be usable before that UI work lands, ship category_id nullable in this baseline and add the NOT NULL in a follow-up migration once every insert path supplies it. Do not accept the constraint on the current justification — restate the audit to name EssayDialog.tsx:137 and WriterEditor.tsx:363.

defects.what: The same NOT NULL breaks the legacy Writer Editor's "Save Draft" on a brand-new essay: category_id is attached only conditionally and the draft path has no category guard, so the insert omits the column. docs/DECISIONS.md records a decision that this guard should exist on draft saves; it was implemented only in the newer WriterStudio, not in this editor.
defects.evidence: src/components/writer/WriterEditor.tsx:325-344 builds essayData without category_id; :346-349 attaches it only `if (categoryId)`, and categoryId initialises to '' at :134 for a new essay. The validation gate at :289 fires only when `targetStatus === 'published'`, and the "Save Draft" button at :509-517 is enabled unconditionally (`disabled={isSaving}`) and calls handleSave('draft') at :511, reaching the insert at :363-367. The create path is routed and reachable: src/App.tsx:201 maps /admin/writer/:section/:slug to WriterEditorPage, src/pages/WriterEditorPage.tsx:8 sets `isNew = slug === 'new'` and passes initialSlug undefined, WriterEditor.tsx:155-158 then returns early leaving essayDbId null, and src/components/writer/WriterList.tsx:165 and :240 both navigate to `/admin/writer/${section}/new`. Contrast src/domains/writing/WriterStudio.tsx:263-273, which does have the guard with the comment "essays.category_id is NOT NULL with an FK RESTRICT ... Validate up-front on every save (not just publish)" — that is the path the author verified. Reproduced against the applied DDL as admin: `ERROR: null value in column "category_id" ... violates not-null constraint`.

defects.what: The file's headline guard against historical failure (a) does not hold. Every admin check is an inline `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.user_roles ...)`. That subquery is itself evaluated under user_roles' OWN RLS, and the user_roles policy set the rebuild is reconstructed from contains a `FOR ALL` policy whose expression calls `public.has_role()`. So a future `REVOKE EXECUTE ON has_role` re-creates the exact outage the header claims immunity from — for every signed-in user, not just admins. The file lists only two prerequisites on the user_roles agent (SELECT grant, own-row SELECT policy) and misses the third and decisive one: user_roles must have no policy that calls a function anon/authenticated could lose EXECUTE on.
defects.evidence: Candidate header asserts: "no policy below references has_role(). Every admin check is inlined as an EXISTS over public.user_roles. That makes the policies immune to any future grant/revoke on has_role()." But supabase/migrations/_archive/20251223113138_7f971e9c-4d54-42dc-8122-b9939721a56e.sql:33-42 defines user_roles' only two policies as `"Users can view their own roles" FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id)` and `"Only admins can manage roles" ON public.user_roles FOR ALL USING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), 'admin'))` — the second has no TO clause, so it applies to SELECT for anon and authenticated. No later archived migration alters user_roles' policies (grep over supabase/migrations/_archive/*.sql for user_roles + policy returns only the ENABLE RLS line in 20251223113138 and a comment in 20260627190000:27); docs/db/import.sql:17-42 bundles the same definition. REPRODUCED on PostgreSQL 16.13: I applied the candidate SQL verbatim on top of stubs plus that exact user_roles policy pair, then ran `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.has_role(uuid, app_role) FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC`. Result: anon `SELECT slug FROM essays` still returned the published row (good), but as authenticated admin `SELECT slug FROM public.essays` -> `ERROR: permission denied for function has_role`; as authenticated NON-admin the same read of a published essay -> `ERROR: permission denied for function has_role`; admin `UPDATE public.essays` -> same error; and AuthContext.tsx:25-30's own-role probe (`select role from user_roles where user_id=$me and role='admin'`) -> same error. The OR with the own-row policy does not save it: the EXECUTE ACL check happens at expression-init time, before any row is evaluated. The author's own regression test passed vacuously because their stub of user_roles carried only the own-row policy (decision note: "stubbed the prerequisites another agent owns ... user_roles + its own-row RLS policy").
defects.fix: Either (a) add the missing third prerequisite as an enforced contract — the user_roles baseline's admin-manage policy must also be inlined (or split so no SELECT-applicable policy on user_roles calls a function), and assert it in this file with a DO block that fails if any pg_policies row on user_roles contains 'has_role'; or (b) stop pretending independence: keep `public.has_role(...)` in the policies and permanently grant EXECUTE to anon, authenticated (which is what 20260627190000 restored), so there is one dependency instead of a hidden transitive one. Do not leave the header claim as written — it is false in the configuration the sibling migration will ship.

defects.what: The claimed "second, independent barrier" at the grant layer does not exist on a real Supabase project, and the decision note that verified it is wrong. A GRANT is additive — it cannot cancel the ALL that Supabase's project-level default privileges already conferred on anon/authenticated for every new table in `public`. RLS is the only barrier (it does hold in every case I probed), so nothing leaks today; but the file records a defense-in-depth layer that is not there, including the "append-only" reasoning for admin_audit_log.
defects.evidence: Candidate section 7 claims "anon is never granted a write privilege at all -- a second, independent barrier behind the 'no anon write policy' rule", and the decision record claims "Verified: anon INSERT on every table fails at the grant layer, before RLS is even reached." Repo evidence that default privileges are in play: no archived migration ever GRANTs anything on a public table (grep over supabase/migrations/_archive/*.sql), yet anon reads essays/sections/categories/books_uploads on the live site — the privileges come from `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon, authenticated, service_role`, which Supabase's bootstrap installs. REPRODUCED with that default in place, then applying the candidate's GRANT block verbatim: `information_schema.role_table_grants` reports anon holding DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE on public.essays (and the same on user_roles for authenticated, despite this file granting only SELECT); anon INSERT into essays/sections/categories/books_uploads/admin_audit_log/council_sessions is rejected with `new row violates row-level security policy`, i.e. by RLS, never `permission denied for table`; anon `SELECT count(*) FROM public.admin_audit_log` and `FROM public.council_sessions` return 0 rather than a table-permission error, so anon does reach RLS on the two tables the file intended to keep behind the grant layer. Likewise the append-only claim: authenticated retains UPDATE/DELETE privileges, so admin UPDATE/DELETE on admin_audit_log silently affects 0 rows (verified: `UPDATE 0`, `DELETE 0`, row still present) instead of failing with "permission denied for table" as the decision note states — append-only comes from the missing policies, not the missing grant. Note also that TRUNCATE, which RLS does not gate at all, is among the privileges anon keeps (not reachable through PostgREST, but the barrier claimed against it does not exist).
defects.fix: If the second barrier is actually wanted, make it explicit: after the GRANT block add `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON public.sections, public.categories, public.essays, public.books_uploads FROM anon; REVOKE ALL ON public.admin_audit_log, public.council_sessions FROM anon; REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON public.admin_audit_log FROM authenticated;`. Otherwise delete the "second, independent barrier" sentence and the "fails at the grant layer" decision note so the record does not overstate the protection.

defects.what: Section 7's grant model is a no-op on managed Supabase, so the "second, independent barrier" it claims does not exist — and the append-only guarantee on admin_audit_log does not hold against TRUNCATE. Two of the recorded "Verified" decisions are false on the real target because the local harness lacked Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (the same class of unfaithful-stub error as the is_local bug the author already caught).
defects.evidence:
EXECUTABILITY FIRST — the file itself is clean. I applied it verbatim (every statement plus every comment block, lexed separately) to a fresh PostgreSQL 16 cluster with the declared prerequisites stubbed, in the order given, psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1: zero errors. Then applied the repo's real seed on top, /home/user/dikagustiana.com/supabase/migrations/20260731235900_seed_surviving_content.sql: zero errors, 8 sections / 1 category / 106 essays (105 draft + 1 published) / 49 finance_modules, and its own post-seed assertions passed. Every hunt-list item checked negative: dependency order is correct (sections -> categories -> essays -> council_sessions; the only external FK targets are the declared public.finance_modules and auth.users); 23 policies, all names distinct within their table; no policy references a nonexistent column; no trigger precedes its table; no storage.* / auth.* ALTER or GRANT; no extension needed (gen_random_uuid is built-in since PG13); `date`, `mode`, `action`, `content`, `status`, `year`, `metadata`, `changes` are all col_name/unreserved and parse unquoted; `REFERENCES auth.users (id)` and `created_by uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT auth.uid()` are both already proven on this project's live history (_archive/20260622140914_af61f445-a261-473a-a526-352c829fcf4b.sql:3 and _archive/20260704080000_create_council_sessions.sql:15). I also confirmed the file's subtlest claim: after `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.validate_essay_tone_fields() FROM PUBLIC`, an authenticated INSERT and UPDATE on essays still fired the trigger successfully while a direct `SELECT public.validate_essay_tone_fields()` was denied — trigger firing genuinely does not check EXECUTE.

THE DEFECT is in Section 7. Managed Supabase ships `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO postgres, anon, authenticated, service_role` in its base image, so every `CREATE TABLE public.*` in this file *immediately* grants DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE to anon and authenticated. A later GRANT adds nothing and removes nothing. Proof from this repo that the live project relied on exactly those defaults: across all 46 files in supabase/migrations/_archive/, `public.sections`, `public.categories` and `public.essays` receive ZERO grant statements — the only GRANTs anywhere are _archive/20260622140914_*.sql:20-21 for admin_audit_log — yet the public site read essays as `anon` through PostgREST for months. The only mechanism that can explain that is the default privileges.

Reproduced on a second database seeded with that one ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES line and then this file:
  - information_schema.role_table_grants shows `anon` holding DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE on public.essays, public.admin_audit_log AND public.user_roles.
  - anon INSERT into essays fails with `new row violates row-level security policy for table "essays"`, NOT `permission denied for table`. So the decision note "Verified: anon INSERT on every table fails at the grant layer, before RLS is even reached" is false on the target; RLS is the only thing stopping it.
  - As an admin, `UPDATE public.admin_audit_log SET action='forged'` returns `UPDATE 0` and `DELETE FROM public.admin_audit_log` returns `DELETE 0` — no error. So the note "Verified: admin UPDATE and DELETE both fail with 'permission denied for table'" is also false on the target.
  - The one that actually bites: RLS does not gate TRUNCATE. As `authenticated` with a NON-ADMIN uid, `DELETE FROM public.essays` correctly returned `DELETE 0`, but `TRUNCATE public.admin_audit_log` SUCCEEDED and emptied the table (count 0). The same applies to essays, sections, categories, council_sessions and books_uploads.

The offending lines are the comment that states the guarantee — `-- also means anon is never granted a write privilege at all -- a second,` / `-- independent barrier behind the "no anon write policy" rule above.` — together with `GRANT SELECT ON public.essays TO anon;`, `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON public.admin_audit_log TO authenticated;` and `-- granted -- no anon policy references user_roles.` above `GRANT SELECT ON public.user_roles TO authenticated;`.

Scope limit, stated honestly: there is NO read leak. anon SELECT on admin_audit_log, council_sessions and user_roles all returned 0 rows (policies are `TO authenticated`, so anon has no applicable policy), and anon saw only the 1 published essay out of 106 after the real seed — failure (b) does not regress. PostgREST never issues TRUNCATE, so the TRUNCATE hole is not reachable with just an anon/authenticated JWT over the REST surface. This is a claimed control that is absent, plus a genuinely weaker append-only guarantee — not a draft leak.
defects.fix:
Add explicit REVOKEs at the top of Section 7, BEFORE the GRANT block, so the file actually owns the privilege state it documents:

REVOKE ALL ON public.sections, public.categories, public.essays,
              public.admin_audit_log, public.council_sessions, public.books_uploads
  FROM anon, authenticated;

Then leave the existing GRANT lines exactly as they are — they become meaningful rather than decorative, anon really does end up SELECT-only, authenticated really does lose UPDATE/DELETE on admin_audit_log, and TRUNCATE is removed from every table so the append-only trail survives a non-admin. Also add `REVOKE ALL ON public.user_roles FROM anon;` next to the existing `GRANT SELECT ON public.user_roles TO authenticated;` to make that comment true. Separately, correct the two decision notes: on managed Supabase anon INSERT and admin UPDATE/DELETE are stopped by RLS, not by the grant layer — and re-run the acceptance matrix on a harness that includes `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO postgres, anon, authenticated, service_role`, since without that line the stub is not the target.
